messages.subject: Extracting raw data before normalization
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to check the quality of Human Exon 1.0 ST arrays before
and after normalization. I am using the HuEx-1_0-st-
v2,coreR3,A20071112,EP.cdf file. When I use: raw <- extractMatrix
(csBC,verbose=verbose), I have got the following error messg:

20090421 16:31:08|Getting data for the array set...
20090421 16:31:08| Allocating matrix...
Error in matrix(naValue, nrow = ncells, ncol = nbrOfArrays) :
cannot allocate vector of length 825753600
20090421 16:31:08| Allocating matrix...done
20090421 16:31:08|Getting data for the array set...done

It seems that I don't have enough memory (I am using macpro with 4GB
RAM). Is there any alternate ways to compare probe intensity values
before and after normalization? BTW, where can I find the
documentation of function: extractMatrix?

Thanks in advance.

Kind regards,
Anbarasu

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Extracting raw data before normalization
parts:
Hi Anbarasu,
You can do a few things. With plotDensity, you can plot the density of
the probes before and after. You can also do image plots of the before
and after. Or you can pull up the raw residuals for groups of genes
(rather than all of them at a time) using readUnits on the before and
after objects.
Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Extracting raw data before normalization
parts:
Hi Anbarasu.

You can find out more about extractMatrix() and readUnits() via the
following:

?extractMatrix.AffymetrixCelSet

?readUnits.AffymetrixCelFile

For quality assessment, you might also look at RLE and NUSE plots from
the PLM fits.

For extractMatrix(), maybe you only want to pull out intensities just
the core probes. If you call extractMatrix() with 'cells=NULL' (the
default), you are trying to read ALL probes and all samples into
memory. Back of the envelope calculation (6M probes, 150 samples, 8
byte float):

> 6000000*150*8/1024^2
[1] 6866.455

is nearly 7GB, plus a little bit of overhead. So, it's no surprise
that that won't fly on your 4G machine. However, maybe you just want
the ~1M core probes (or even a random sampling). One way to do this
with extractMatrix() is:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,
tag="coreR3,A20071112,EP")

# get the indices of just the core probesets
cellIndices <- getCellIndices(cdf, unlist=TRUE, useNames=FALSE)

# extract data for only these probes (about 8MB of memory per sample)
d <- extractMatrix(cs, cells=cellIndices,verbose=-50)

... could do boxplots of intensity:

boxplot( as.data.frame(log2(d)) )

.... or maybe 100K probes is enough to get a feel for what the samples
are doing ...

s <- sample(cellIndices, 100000)

# extract data for only these probes (about 750KB of memory per sample)
d <- extractMatrix(cs, cells=s,verbose=-50)

.... and replace 'cs' above here with 'csBC', 'csN', or whatever
AffymetrixCelSet object you are interested in.

Just some thoughts.

Hope that helps.
Mark

Yes, you should see the same thing with 1M probes. Is this a problem? I
don't know. It does look a little different than the example in our paper
(Figure 1):

http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2105/10/110

But, you could have a completely different experimental situation (a high
proportion of genes expressed) or different protocols (rRNA reduction?),
but I don't have a good feel for how this all affects the data.

Cheers,
